title: Integrated Shield Plan premium increases, rider changes and claims handling
asked: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how MOH addresses insurers raising base Integrated Shield Plan premiums, ensures claims are not unreasonably rejected, and whether it will mandate premium transparency and penalise unjustifiable hikes. Dr Hamid Razak asked whether MOH knew insurers intended to raise base IP premiums alongside the 1 April 2026 rider changes and what analysis was done on the interaction.
asked_by: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Dr Hamid Razak
response: Ms Rahayu Mahzam said IP insurers review premiums yearly, and from December 2021 to December 2024 private hospital IP premiums rose an average 8.6% a year while rider premiums rose 17.2% a year. She said some private hospital IP and rider plans were recently repriced, but switching to new riders can save policyholders 35% to 40%. MOH regulates key parameters like co-payment and deductible but generally does not intervene in insurers' commercial decisions such as premium setting; MAS and MOH require fair claims handling, 30 days' notice of policy changes, and FIDReC for disputes. She also said premium increases reflect underlying healthcare cost pressures, and MOH is addressing root causes through fee benchmarks, clinical guidance, enforcement, rider reforms and not-for-profit private hospitals.

key_points.point: IP insurers review premiums of IPs and riders every year.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurers review the premiums of IPs and riders every year.

key_points.point: From December 2021 to December 2024, private hospital IP premiums rose an average 8.6% a year and rider premiums rose 17.2% a year.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: private hospital IP premiums have been rising every year at an average of 8.6% while private hospital rider premiums have been rising every year at an average of 17.2%.

key_points.point: Some private hospital IP and rider plans were recently repriced.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: some private hospital IP and rider plans were recently repriced.

key_points.point: Policyholders can save on average 35% to 40% in premiums by switching to the new riders.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: policyholders can save on average 35% to 40% premiums by switching to the new riders.

key_points.point: IPs and riders are private commercial products that supplement MediShield Life for unsubsidised healthcare.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: IPs and riders are private, commercial products that supplement MediShield Life coverage for unsubsidised healthcare.

key_points.point: MOH regulates key parameters like co-payment and deductible but generally does not intervene in insurers' commercial decisions such as premium setting.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: MOH's general practice is not to intervene in insurers' commercial decisions, such as the setting of premiums.

key_points.point: Insurers must notify policyholders of any change in policy terms and conditions at least 30 days before it takes effect.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: insurers must notify their policyholders of any change in policy terms and conditions at least 30 days before it takes effect.

key_points.point: Policyholders can take claim disputes to FIDReC.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: policyholders can take it to the Financial Industry Disputes Resolution Centre (FIDReC)

key_points.point: MAS will take action against insurers if they do not pay claims according to policy terms or have unfair claims handling practices.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: MAS will also take action against insurers if they do not pay claims in accordance with policy terms and conditions or have unfair claims handling practices.

key_points.point: Premium increases reflect underlying healthcare cost increases.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: the premium increase actually reflects the underlying healthcare cost increases

key_points.point: Artificially limiting premium increases would not be sustainable.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: if we artificially limit it, it will not be sustainable.

key_points.point: MOH uses fee benchmarks, clinical guidance, enforcement against errant providers, rider reforms and not-for-profit private hospitals to moderate increases.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: fee benchmarks, clinical guidance to ensure that appropriate care is given and we enforce against errant providers.

key_points.point: Seniors can review or right-size their coverage and consider cheaper riders.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Seniors can, at the appropriate juncture, review or right-size their coverage in accordance to their needs as well as to their affordability at that moment in time.

key_points.point: MOH assures that no one will be left out of access to healthcare, anchored by subsidised public healthcare and the S+3M framework.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: no one will be left out or not have access to healthcare

key_points.point: MOH is reviewing whether to put benchmarks on other components of private healthcare costs.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We are reviewing to see if there is a need and if there are some ways for us to also put in benchmarks in the other components of the other costs.

key_points.point: Panel arrangements are described as an enduring market reaction to cost pressure on insurers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: This remains something that will be an enduring feature because this is a market reaction to something that is causing a pressure on the insurer's part.

key_points.point: MOH is mindful about where it intervenes because insurers need to remain competitive and there is a commercial dimension.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we are very mindful about where we intervene

left_open: Whether MOH will mandate greater transparency in how insurers calculate premiums
Whether MOH will publicly penalise insurers for unjustifiable price hikes
Whether MOH was aware of insurers' intention to raise base IP premiums at the same time as the 1 April 2026 rider changes
Whether any analysis was done on how base premium increases would interact with rider changes
Whether MOH has considered policy levers to incentivise insurers to pass administrative cost savings to consumers as lower premiums
Whether panel arrangements have equitably kept doctors' fee sizes manageable compared to fee benchmarks
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on premium increase limits, safeguards for seniors, private healthcare cost components, panel arrangements and insurer cost savings.

_dropped.point: MAS and MOH require insurers to uphold contractual obligations and process claims fairly.
_dropped.quote: MAS and MOH require insurance companies to uphold their contractual obligations and proces
